context:
You asked for visuals (10:55 CST). Each option now has its mockup, drawn on the folded Duo (466 pt wide), with extra pictures for a tap on "0 stamped" and for the open Duo.
Goal: the phone's order stamps look and work like the web's.
Problem (goal): step 6 ships two choices the mockup didn't have. The note field is two lines tall where the mockup shows one, so it fits the 44-point tap minimum at larger text sizes. And the "0 stamped" filter cell is disabled when nothing is stamped, but it is not greyed out: its button style dims only on press, so it looks active and does nothing. Both depart from the mockup, so they need your word.
Based on (read): the step 6 design review.
Based on (ruling): house rule ux-house-rules-govern: tap targets at least 44 points.
Based on (read): the step 6 mockup is not in the repo, so option b is drawn from this item's own description and the web's one-line note field.
Departs from: main ships a two-line note field and a dead "0 stamped" cell — option b changes them to a one-line field and an always-active cell, as the step 6 mockup had.
Meanwhile: step 6 ships with both. A change later is a small edit.

options.gain: The note field is easy to tap, and the filter can't show an empty list.
options.how: A two-line note field, and a "0 stamped" cell that looks active but does nothing.
options.label: Keep both
options.lose: It differs a little from the mockup, and the dead cell gives no sign that it is off.

options.gain: It looks like the step 6 mockup and the web.
options.how: A one-line note field with a taller tap area; "0 stamped" always active.
options.label: Match the mockup
options.lose: More work. Tapping "0 stamped" shows an empty list.

title: The phone's stamp editor: a two-line note field and a "0 stamped" cell that looks active but does nothing. Keep both?
why: Both follow the house tap-size rule, and neither can show you a dead end.
